title: Identification of Potential Biomarkers Associated with Spermatogenesis in Azoospermia.
authors: Li, ChaoCheng; Li, MengYu; Liu, YaXing; Li, Jian; Zhang, YaRu; Wang, Hui; Zhang, YongSheng; Jia, Bin
one_liner_zh: 该研究基于GEO表达数据筛选无精子症精子发生相关生物标志物，虽含转录因子调控网络分析，但核心为差异表达与诊断标志物，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Azoospermia, characterized by the absence of spermatozoa in the ejaculate, affects approximately 1% of all men and 10 - 15% of infertile males, representing the most severe form of male infertility. It is classified into obstructive azoospermia (OA) and nonobstructive azoospermia (NOA), with the latter often resulting from unexplained failures in spermatogenesis. This study endeavored to clarify the molecular underpinnings of sper-matogenesis in NOA and to identify viable therapeutic targets. METHODS: We analyzed expression data from NOA and normal spermatogenesis samples obtained from the GEO database. Differential expression analysis was performed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs). We then intersected these DEGs with genes known to be related to spermatogenesis to pinpoint spermatogenesis-related DEGs specific to NOA. Subsequent analyses, including gene ontology (GO) and Kyoto encyclopedia of genes and genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichments, aimed to elucidate potential signaling pathways involved. A protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was constructed to highlight hub genes, whose diagnostic potential was assessed by using ROC curve analysis. Additionally, miRNA and transcription factor (TF) regulatory network for hub genes were analyzed. The efficacy of identified hub genes as biomarkers was validated through RT-qPCR and Western blotting in a mouse model of NOA. RESULTS: This study identified 68 NOV-specific spermatogenesis-related genes. Enrichment analyses in GO and KEGG pathways highlighted their involvement in cellular processes related to reproduction in multicellular organism and endocrine and other factor-regulated calcium reabsorption. Seven hub genes were identified, with ROC curve analysis affirming their significant diagnostic value. Constructed networks revealed intricate interactions among miRNAs, hub genes, and TFs. CONCLUSIONS: We identified seven hub genes (CATSPER1, CATSPER3, CATSPER4, CATSPERG, OAZ3, ODF1, and SUN5) significantly associated with spermatogenesis in NOA, demonstrating their potential as biomarkers for diagnosing and monitoring the disease.
abstract_zh: 背景：无精子症（Azoospermia）以射精中缺乏精子为特征，影响约1%的男性和10-15%的不育男性，是男性不育最严重的形式。其分为梗阻性无精子症（OA）和非梗阻性无精子症（NOA），后者通常源于原因不明的精子发生失败。本研究旨在阐明NOA中精子发生的分子机制，并识别可行的治疗靶点。方法：我们分析了从GEO数据库获取的NOA和正常精子发生样本的表达数据。进行差异表达分析以识别差异表达基因（DEGs）。随后，我们将这些DEGs与已知与精子发生相关的基因相交，以定位NOA特异性的精子发生相关DEGs。后续分析，包括基因本体论（GO）和京都基因与基因组百科全书（KEGG）通路富集，旨在阐明可能涉及的信号通路。构建了蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络以突出枢纽基因，并通过ROC曲线分析评估其诊断潜力。此外，分析了枢纽基因的miRNA和转录因子（TF）调控网络。通过RT-qPCR和Western blotting在NOA小鼠模型中验证了所识别枢纽基因作为生物标志物的有效性。结果：本研究识别了68个NOA特异性精子发生相关基因。GO和KEGG通路富集分析强调了它们在多细胞生物生殖相关细胞过程以及内分泌和其他因子调节的钙重吸收中的参与。识别出七个枢纽基因，ROC曲线分析确认了它们显著的诊断价值。构建的网络揭示了miRNA、枢纽基因和TF之间的复杂相互作用。结论：我们识别了七个与NOA精子发生显著相关的枢纽基因（CATSPER1、CATSPER3、CATSPER4、CATSPERG、OAZ3、ODF1和SUN5），证明了它们作为诊断和监测该疾病的生物标志物的潜力。
